items.followUp: What is meant by zero correction of a screw gauge?

rubric.why: Identifies the position that produces positive zero error.
rubric.how: State that, with the screw gauge closed, the circular-scale zero lies below the reference line.

rubric.why: Identifies the position that produces negative zero error.
rubric.how: State that, with the screw gauge closed, the circular-scale zero lies above the reference line.

modelAnswer: When the screw gauge is closed, positive zero error occurs if the zero of the circular scale lies below the reference line.
Negative zero error occurs if the zero of the circular scale lies above the reference line.

items.followUp: State the condition for an object to move with uniform speed.

rubric.why: Gives the defining distance-time condition for uniform speed.
rubric.how: Mention equal distances covered in equal time intervals.

rubric.why: Contrasts variable speed with uniform speed.
rubric.how: State that the speed changes with time, or that unequal distances are covered in equal time intervals.

modelAnswer: An object has uniform speed if it covers equal distances in equal intervals of time.
An object has variable speed if its speed changes with time.

items.followUp: What force is required to give a 2 kg mass an acceleration of 3 m/s²?

rubric.why: Identifies the SI unit of force.
States the defining force-acceleration relation for one newton.
rubric.how: Explain that 1 N gives a 1 kg mass an acceleration of 1 m/s².

modelAnswer: The SI unit of force is the newton (N).
One newton is the force that produces an acceleration of 1 m/s² in a mass of 1 kg.

items.followUp: What happens to the extension of a spring when the applied force is doubled, within its elastic limit?

rubric.why: States the proportional relationship in Hooke’s law.
rubric.how: Say that extension is directly proportional to applied force.

rubric.why: Includes the condition or formula that completes the law.
rubric.how: State that the law holds within the elastic limit and write F = kx (or F ∝ x).

modelAnswer: Within the elastic limit, the extension of a spring is directly proportional to the applied force.
F = kx, where F is the applied force, x is the extension and k is the spring constant.

items.followUp: How much heat is needed to raise the temperature of 2 kg of a substance with specific heat capacity 500 J kg⁻¹ °C⁻¹ by 3°C?

rubric.why: Identifies specific heat as a heat quantity per unit mass and temperature change.
rubric.how: Describe it as the heat required to raise a substance’s temperature.

rubric.why: Gives the reference mass and temperature rise in the definition.
rubric.description: States the unit-mass and temperature-rise conditions.
rubric.how: Specify a 1 kg mass and a temperature rise of 1°C (or 1 K).

modelAnswer: Specific heat capacity of a substance is the heat required to raise the temperature of 1 kg of that substance by 1°C (or 1 K).

items.followUp: What is meant by nuclear fission?

rubric.why: Identifies nuclear physics as a branch of physics.
rubric.description: Names the field as a branch of physics.
rubric.how: State that nuclear physics is a branch of physics.

rubric.why: Identifies the subject matter of nuclear physics.
rubric.how: Mention the study of atomic nuclei and their properties or processes.

modelAnswer: Nuclear physics is the branch of physics that deals with the study of atomic nuclei, their properties and the processes occurring in them.

items.followUp: Name one source of error that can affect a reading on a beam balance.

rubric.why: Notes that a digital balance presents a direct electronic reading.
rubric.how: Mention that the balance displays the measured value electronically as digits.

rubric.why: Explains that a digital reading reduces errors associated with reading a beam balance.
rubric.how: State that it avoids or reduces reading/parallax error involved in reading a beam and pointer.

modelAnswer: A digital electronic balance displays the measured value directly as digits.
This avoids reading and parallax errors that may occur when reading a beam balance, so its measurement is more accurate.

items.followUp: Which branch of mechanics studies the forces responsible for motion?

rubric.why: Identifies kinematics as a branch of mechanics.
rubric.how: State that kinematics is a branch of mechanics.

rubric.why: Distinguishes kinematics by its focus on motion without its causes.
rubric.how: Explain that it describes motion without considering the forces or causes producing it.

modelAnswer: Kinematics is the branch of mechanics that describes the motion of objects without considering the forces or causes producing that motion.
